answer_sql:
WITH first_order AS (
  SELECT
    customer_key,
    MIN(order_date) AS first_order_date
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line
  GROUP BY
    customer_key
), labelled AS (
  SELECT
    customer_key,
    first_order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE) AS is_new,
    CASE
      WHEN first_order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
      THEN 'new customers with first order from 2024 onwards'
      ELSE 'customers older then 2024'
    END AS customer_group
  FROM first_order
)
SELECT
  l.customer_group,
  ROUND(SUM(s.net_amount), 2) AS revenue
FROM labelled AS l
JOIN contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS s
  ON s.customer_key = l.customer_key
GROUP BY
  l.customer_group,
  l.is_new
ORDER BY
  l.is_new DESC

body.value: Two rows, read straight off the result. The 10,797 customers whose first ever order fell on or after 1 January 2024 have brought in 25,771,089.77 USD; the 41,392 customers who had already ordered before 2024 have brought in 193,043,381.89 USD. Both are NET revenue — after discount — and each covers that group's ENTIRE order history, across shops and the web shop together, on orders placed between 2016-05-18 and 2025-12-31, the full extent the bundle holds. The two sum to 218,814,471.66, which is every sale in the warehouse, so nothing is lost or counted twice. WHAT I DID NOT INCLUDE, and what a reader should know before comparing the two numbers: the groups are not measured over a common window — the new group has only two years of history to its name while the older group's figure carries nine extra years of buying, so most of the 7.5x gap is elapsed time, not spending behaviour. Over the same two years (orders placed from 2024 onwards) the same two groups give 25,771,089.77 against 35,146,090.74. Also excluded: the 52,801 people on the register who have never ordered, who have no first order date and so fall in neither group; and anything before discount — gross would be 27,378,654.15 and 205,222,888.51.

turns.why: Project the two columns the question asked for, ordered as the question phrases them — new customers first, then older — with the figures already measured and reconciled against the bundle's declared total.
turns.did:
WITH first_order AS (
  SELECT
    customer_key,
    MIN(order_date) AS first_order_date
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line
  GROUP BY
    customer_key
), labelled AS (
  SELECT
    customer_key,
    first_order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE) AS is_new,
    CASE
      WHEN first_order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
      THEN 'new customers with first order from 2024 onwards'
      ELSE 'customers older then 2024'
    END AS customer_group
  FROM first_order
)
SELECT
  l.customer_group,
  ROUND(SUM(s.net_amount), 2) AS revenue
FROM labelled AS l
JOIN contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS s
  ON s.customer_key = l.customer_key
GROUP BY
  l.customer_group,
  l.is_new
ORDER BY
  l.is_new DESC
